title: Prophylactic Onlay Mesh versus Suture Only (PROMSO Trial) – Reduction of Incisional Hernia Incidence After Open Abdominal Surgery Through Implantation of a Prophylactic Alloplastic Mesh in Onlay Position
summary:
After treatment with an open abdomen (laparostomy), patients frequently develop an incisional hernia, which is a weakness or defect in the abdominal wall at the site of the surgical incision. This complication may cause discomfort, limit physical function, and often requires additional surgical repair.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether placing a prophylactic surgical mesh on the abdominal wall at the time of definitive abdominal closure can reduce the incidence of incisional hernia.

Two treatment strategies will be compared. In one group, patients receive a resorbable surgical mesh in addition to standard abdominal wall closure. In the other group, abdominal closure is performed according to current guidelines without mesh implantation.

Participants will be followed over several years to evaluate the occurrence of incisional hernias as well as postoperative complications, pain, quality of life, and return to work.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent for study participation provided by the patient or, if the patient is temporarily incapable of consent, by a legal representative.

Age ≥ 18 years.

Open abdomen treatment (laparostomy) following a complete midline laparotomy (from the xiphoid to at least 5 cm above the symphysis).

Planned complete tension-free fascial closure along the entire length of the incision.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of informed consent for study participation.

Incomplete fascial closure.

Wound class CDC III or IV.

Septic intra-abdominal process or peritonitis as the indication for open abdomen treatment (laparostomy).
